structure.proved_step: LEMMA (repair of G0046, all supports). Let w in Z^n have support S with |S| = s >= 1 and 1 <= |w_i| <= K on S. Let F be a uniform random k-subset of [n], b uniform on the coordinates outside F, and g = [w.x >= t] for any integer t. Then E_F Pr_b[g non-constant] <= (sqrt2*K + 2/sqrt(n)) * k/sqrt(n). Proof: (1) g is non-constant iff V = sum over i outside F of w_i b_i lies in a half-open window of integer length L = sum over i in F of |w_i| <= K*j, where j = |S cap F|, so the window holds at most K*j integers. (2) Let N = s - j be the number of fixed support variables. After replacing b_i by 1-b_i where w_i < 0, the N weights are positive integers and subsets with equal sum form an antichain, so Sperner gives Pr[V=v] <= C(N, floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N) for N >= 1. Hence Pr_b[non-constant | F] <= min(1, K*j/sqrt(s-j)) for j < s. (3) On the event j <= s/2: the bound is <= sqrt2*K*j/sqrt(s), and E[j] = s*k/n gives E of this term <= sqrt2*K*sqrt(s)*k/n <= sqrt2*K*k/sqrt(n). (4) On the event j > s/2 (this includes j = s, i.e. N = 0) use the trivial bound 1 and Markov: P(j >= s/2) <= E[j]/(s/2) = 2k/n = (2/sqrt(n))*k/sqrt(n). Adding (3) and (4) gives the claim. Constant gates (s = 0) contribute 0. The bound is independent of t.

structure.proved_step: statement: Finite-family exhaustive selector lemma. Let T be a Boolean truth table of length N, let C_s be a finite family of circuit encodings with |C_s| <= 2^{b(s)}, and let V(T,C) be a deterministic verifier that decides whether tt(C^A)=T in time at most v(N,s) for every C in C_s. If some C in C_s satisfies V(T,C)=1, lexicographic exhaustive search returns a satisfying C in at most 2^{b(s)} verifier calls and time at most 2^{b(s)}v(N,s) plus encoding overhead. Proof: enumerate C_s in lexicographic order, run V on each encoding, and return the first accepting encoding. Finiteness and the assumed existence of an accepting encoding imply termination and correctness. Scope: this gives no QE* resource bound unless 2^{b(s)}v(N,s) fits it, and establishes no reduction or P-versus-NP consequence.

structure.lemma: Restriction lemma (exact). Let g(x) = [w.x >= t] on {0,1}^n with integer weights w, S+(F) = sum_{i in F, w_i>0} w_i, S-(F) = sum_{i in F, w_i<0} w_i, for a free set F. Fix the other variables by rho in {0,1}^{[n]\F}, and set c = sum_{i not in F} w_i rho_i. Then g restricted by rho is non-constant iff S-(F) < t - c <= S+(F). Proof: on the free cube, w.x restricted equals c + sum_{i in F} w_i x_i, a linear function whose minimum and maximum over {0,1}^F are attained at the vertices x_i = [w_i<0] and x_i = [w_i>0], with values c+S-(F) and c+S+(F). g is constant 1 iff min >= t, constant 0 iff max < t, so non-constant iff min < t <= max. Consequence: a restriction shifts every threshold by c and shrinks the window to width W_F = sum_{i in F} |w_i|; a bottom gate survives the restriction iff its shifted threshold lies in the window.

structure.lemma: Theorem C (bounded-weight switching bound for one bottom THR gate). Setting: g(x)=[sum_i w_i x_i >= t] on {0,1}^n, integer weights, nz = number of nonzero weights, M = max|w_i| >= 1. Random restriction R_p: each variable free independently with probability p, otherwise fixed to 0 or 1 with probability (1-p)/2 each. Claim: for 0 < p <= 1/4, P(restricted g is non-constant) <= exp(-p nz/3) + 2 sqrt(2) M p sqrt(nz). Corollary: p = 1/(16 M sqrt(nz)) with sqrt(nz) >= 126 M gives P(non-constant) <= 1/4. Proof: Lemma A (Sperner): for nonzero integers a_1..a_k and uniform eps in {0,1}^k, P(sum a_i eps_i = v) <= C(k, floor(k/2))/2^k <= 1/sqrt(k) for every v (flip eps_i where a_i<0; the sets with a given sum form an antichain). Lemma B: given the free set F, the non-constancy window of the restriction lemma has W_F integers, so P(non-constant | F) <= W_F/sqrt(k) <= M s/sqrt(k), with s = number of free nonzero-weight variables and k = nz - s >= 1. Chernoff: P(s > 2 p nz) <= exp(-p nz/3). On s <= 2 p nz (and p <= 1/4) we have k >= nz/2, giving conditional bound 2 sqrt(2) M p sqrt(nz). Take the expectation over s.

structure.lemma: Lemma R1 (Kolmogorov-Rogozin reduction, unbounded weights). Let a_1..a_N be nonzero integers, each j free independently with prob p, F = free set, L_F = sum_{j in F}|a_j|, S_F = sum_{j not in F} min(a_j^2, L_F^2). Then P(gate nonconstant) <= sqrt(8) * A * E_F[min(1, L_F / sqrt(S_F))], where A is the universal Kolmogorov-Rogozin constant. Proof: condition on F. Nonconstancy means X = sum_{j not in F} a_j u_j (u_j iid uniform bits) lies in a window of exactly L_F consecutive integers. Apply Rogozin with L = L_F and L_j = min(|a_j|/2, L). Each X_j = a_j u_j has Q_j(L_j) <= 1/2, since an interval of length < |a_j| contains at most one of {0, a_j}. Hence sum L_j^2 (1 - Q_j) >= (1/8) S_F, which gives the bound.
structure.proved_step: Lemma R1 as stated in the lemma field: Kolmogorov-Rogozin reduction of the unbounded-weight restriction probability to the expectation in F of min(1, L_F/sqrt(S_F)).

structure.lemma: Lemma (sparse-restriction bound, one THR gate). Let g(x) = [Σ_j w_j x_j ≥ t] with integer weights, nz = #{j : w_j ≠ 0} ≥ 2. Choose a uniform k-subset F of variables, with 1 ≤ k ≤ nz/2, and fix the variables outside F to uniform bits. Then P[g restricted is non-constant] ≤ k · ((1/n) Σ_j |w_j|) · √(2/nz). Proof: Let lo = Σ_{j∈F} min(w_j,0), hi = Σ_{j∈F} max(w_j,0), W_F = hi−lo (window width). The restriction is non-constant iff t−hi ≤ c < t−lo where c = Σ_{j∉F} w_j x_j. Given free set F of size k, there are r = #{j∉F : w_j≠0} ≥ nz−k ≥ nz/2 free nonzero weights. Flipping bits where w_j<0 turns c into a sum of r positive integers; sets with fixed sum form an antichain, so by Sperner P[c=v] ≤ C(r,⌊r/2⌋)/2^r ≤ 1/√r for every v. Hence P[non-constant|F] ≤ W_F/√r ≤ W_F·√(2/nz). Since P[j∈F]=k/n, E[W_F]=(k/n)Σ_j|w_j|. Taking expectation over F gives the claim. Consequence: for k=O(1) the undecided fraction is O(k·mean|w|/√n), giving the 1/√n decay; for k=c√n it gives only order c·mean|w|, consistent with measured Θ(1).

structure.proved_step: Lemma (heavy-split restriction bound, repair of G0008). Setting: g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t], integer weights w_j, any integer t, n variables, nz = #{j : w_j != 0}. Fix tau >= 1 and H = #{j : |w_j| > tau}. Let F be a uniform k-subset of variables, 1 <= k <= nz/2, and fix the other variables to uniform bits. Then P[restriction of g is non-constant] <= k*H/n + A*(tau*k + 1)*sqrt(2/(nz - k)), where A is the absolute constant of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin inequality (cited; exact constant and statement to be source-checked). Proof: (1) Let E = {F contains a heavy variable}. P(E) <= E[#heavy in F] = k*H/n by a union bound. (2) On the complement of E, every j in F has |w_j| <= tau, so W_F := sum_{j in F} |w_j| <= tau*k. (3) Given F, the restriction is non-constant iff c := sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j lies in the integer window [t - hi, t - lo), where hi, lo are the positive and negative parts summed over F; this window has W_F integer points. (4) Let r = #{j not in F : w_j != 0} >= nz - k. Each summand w_j x_j takes values 0 and w_j, so its sup-probability on any half-open integer interval of length 1 is at most 1/2. Kolmogorov-Rogozin with scales l_j = 1 gives sup_x P(c in [x, x+L)) <= A*L/sqrt(r/2) for L >= 1; with L = W_F + 1 this is <= A*(W_F+1)*sqrt(2/r) <= A*(tau*k+1)*sqrt(2/(nz-k)) on the complement of E. (5) Combine: P(nonconst) <= P(E) + sup over the complement = k*H/n + A*(tau*k+1)*sqrt(2/(nz-k)). QED (modulo source-check of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin statement). The bound does not depend on the maximum weight M.

structure.proved_step: Lemma (exact unit-weight average, lane C). Let g(x) = [x_1 + ... + x_n >= t] with all weights 1. Let F be a fixed k-subset of the variables, 0 <= k <= n, and let the other m = n-k variables be uniform bits. Let t be uniform on the 2n+1 integers -n..n. Then the average over t of P[restriction of g to F is non-constant] equals exactly k/(2n+1). Proof: let c = sum of the m free bits, so 0 <= c <= m. Let s = number of ones in F, 0 <= s <= k. The restriction is non-constant iff c < t <= c+k, i.e. c in [t-k, t-1]. For each c in [0, m], the number of integers t in [-n, n] with c+1 <= t <= c+k is exactly k, because c >= 0 and c+k <= m+k = n. Summing over t and averaging over c gives k/(2n+1). QED. Consequence: for k = pn the average tends to p/2, not p, so the uniform-t value in S-4c7647ab5f is wrong by a factor 2. The lemma is an identity, not a bound. It does not control the worst-case threshold, which at t near the centre gives an undecided probability of order k/sqrt(n), so it does not close G0001 or G0003.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA R (window bound, arbitrary integer weights, uniform in the threshold). Let g(x)=[sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with w in Z^n, t in Z, nz=#{j: w_j != 0} >= 2, F a uniform random k-subset with 1 <= k <= nz/2, and the bits outside F uniform. Then for EVERY integer t: P[g restricted to F is nonconstant] <= (k/n) * (sum_j |w_j|) * sqrt(2/nz). PROOF. (1) Fix F. Put lo = sum_{j in F} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in F} max(w_j,0), W_F = hi - lo = sum_{j in F}|w_j|, and c = sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j. The restriction is nonconstant iff t - hi <= c < t - lo, i.e. c lies in a window of exactly W_F consecutive integers. (2) Let r = #{j not in F: w_j != 0} >= nz - k >= nz/2. Replace x_j by 1 - x_j for each j not in F with w_j < 0 (a bijection of bit strings). Then c becomes sum_J a_j y_j over r indices with a_j = |w_j| > 0. For each fixed value v, the sets J with sum_{j in J} a_j = v form an antichain (A strictly inside B forces a strictly smaller sum), so by Sperner P[c = v | F] <= C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r). (3) Hence P[nonconstant | F] <= sum over the W_F window values v of P[c=v | F] <= W_F/sqrt(r) <= W_F*sqrt(2/nz). (4) P[j in F] = k/n gives E_F[W_F] = (k/n) sum_j |w_j|. Taking the expectation over F proves the claim. QED. The bound is uniform in t, so it is a worst-case-over-thresholds statement, not an average over t.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (gcd-refined window bound, one THR gate, per fixed free set). Let g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integer weights, F a set of variables, and out = complement of F. Let W_F = sum_{j in F} |w_j| (the window width), r_F = #{j in out : w_j != 0}, and g_F = gcd{|w_j| : j in out, w_j != 0} (assume r_F >= 1). Then, for uniform independent bits on out and any fixed assignment of F, P[g restricted to F is non-constant] <= (floor(W_F/g_F) + 1)/sqrt(r_F). PROOF. (i) Non-constancy: let lo = sum_{j in F} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in F} max(w_j,0). The F-part of the sum takes its minimum lo and maximum hi, so the restriction is non-constant iff t - hi <= c < t - lo, where c = sum_{j in out} w_j x_j. (ii) Sperner: write y_j = x_j if w_j > 0 and y_j = 1 - x_j if w_j < 0. Then c = const + sum_{j in out, w_j != 0} |w_j| y_j with positive integer coefficients a_j = |w_j|. For a fixed value v the set {S : sum_{j in S} a_j = v} is an antichain of subsets of the r_F free positions, so P[c = v] <= C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r) (the central-binomial inequality holds for every r >= 1). (iii) Residue: every a_j is a multiple of g_F, so c takes values only in one residue class mod g_F. The window [t-hi, t-lo) contains W_F consecutive integers, hence at most ceil(W_F/g_F) <= floor(W_F/g_F)+1 values of the correct residue. Summing (ii) over these values gives P[nonconst | F] <= (floor(W_F/g_F)+1)/sqrt(r_F). QED. Consequence: for g_F >= 2 the window term is divided by g_F; for g_F = 1 it reduces to the earlier W_F/sqrt(r) bound up to +1.

structure.lemma: L2-window lemma (per gate, conditional on F). Let g(x)=[sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integer weights, F subset [n] fixed, x_F fixed, x_O uniform in {0,1}^{[n]\F}. Let WF = sum_{j in F}|w_j| >= 1 and Neff(F) = sum_{j not in F, w_j != 0} min(|w_j|, WF)^2. Then P_{x_O}[g|F nonconstant] <= sqrt(2)*A*WF/sqrt(Neff(F)), where A is the absolute constant of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin inequality Q(S;L) <= A*L*(sum_j l_j^2 (1-Q(X_j;l_j)))^{-1/2} (0<l_j<=L). Proof: nonconstancy means the shift c = sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j lies in a window of WF consecutive integers, so the probability is at most Q(c;WF). Take l_j = min(|w_j|, WF) <= WF. The two-point variable X_j = w_j x_j has Q(X_j; l_j) <= 1/2 because an interval of length l_j <= |w_j| contains at most one of {0, w_j}. So sum_j l_j^2 (1-Q_j) >= Neff/2 and the inequality gives the bound. The constant is scale-invariant in w.

structure.lemma: Exact window identity (unit weights, no probability). Let O be a set of N variables with weights w_j in {-1,+1}, N_+ positive and N_- negative. Its outside sum S(x_O) = sum_{j in O} w_j x_j takes exactly the integer values -N_- ... N_+, which are N+1 values. For a base b and threshold t, the gate g = [b + S >= t] is non-constant on {0,1}^O iff min S < t - b <= max S, i.e. iff t - b lies in {-N_- + 1, ..., N_+}. That set has exactly N integers. Proof: the extremes of S are attained at all-zero and all-one-on-the-matching-sign points, and S takes every intermediate integer because each unit step is one variable. Consequence: if P(t - b = v) <= q for every integer v, then P[g non-constant] <= N q. This is an exact identity, not a bound on the top gate, and it is trivial bookkeeping, so it does NOT count as progress and closes nothing.

structure.lemma: Restriction lemma for integer weights (Lemma-B shape with explicit constant). Setting: integer weights w_j, t in Z, a set R of free variables with N=|R| and W_R = sum over R of |w_j|, F = complement of R, k = number of j in F with w_j != 0 (k >= 1), and x_F uniform in {0,1}^F. Claim: P_{x_F}[ g restricted to x_F is non-constant in x_R ] <= W_R * binom(k, floor(k/2)) / 2^k <= W_R / sqrt(k), where g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t]. For unit weights on all of [n] this reads N/sqrt(n-N). Proof. (1) Let S(x_R) = sum over R of w_j x_j, with max mx and min mn, so mx - mn = W_R. Put b = sum over F of w_j x_j. Then g is non-constant iff b + mn < t <= b + mx, i.e. iff t - b lies in the set of integers (mn, mx], which has exactly W_R elements and does not depend on x_F. (2) Write each fixed term w_j x_j = w_j/2 + a_j e_j with a_j = w_j/2 (|a_j| >= 1/2) and e_j = +-1 uniform. Erdos' 1945 Littlewood-Offord theorem (source-check needed) says that at most binom(k, floor(k/2)) of the 2^k sign vectors give a sum in any open interval of length 1 (after scaling by 2: |a'_j| >= 1 and length 2). A point lies in such an interval, so P[b = v] <= binom(k, floor(k/2))/2^k for every integer v. (3) P[nonconst] = P[t - b in (mn, mx]] <= sum over the W_R integers v of P[b = t - v] <= W_R * binom(k, floor(k/2))/2^k. (4) binom(k, floor(k/2))/2^k <= 1/sqrt(k): for k = 2m or 2m+1 this follows from binom(2m,m)/4^m <= 1/sqrt(3m+1) (classical, by induction), since 3m+1 >= 2m. The case k = 1 gives 1/2 <= 1. QED.

structure.lemma: For any THR o THR circuit C whose bottom gates are g_j = [W_j·x ≥ t_j] with W_j ∈ {−1,1}^{n−N} of unit magnitude and a free variable set F of size N = c√n, if the top gate is a THR with weight vector W_top = Σ_{j∈F} W_j and threshold t_top, then the top gate output equals 1 iff Σ_{j∈F} W_j·x ≥ t_top. Consequently the top gate can be decided by computing S = Σ_{j∈F} W_j·x, which requires examining at most N bottom gates and runs in time O(N) = O(√n).
structure.proved_step: Proof: The top gate is the OR of the bottom gate outputs. Each bottom gate's output depends only on the sign of W_j·x. The sum S = Σ_{j∈F} W_j·x aggregates these signs; a positive majority (S ≥ t_top) implies the OR is 1, otherwise 0. Computing S needs to read each of the N bottom gates once, i.e., O(N) time.

structure.lemma: Setting: m integer weight vectors W_j in Z^n, a fixed assignment rho on V minus F (|F| = k) with x_F free, and thresholds t_j drawn uniformly from {-R,...,R} independently of W and rho. Let mn_j = min over x_F of W_j.x and mx_j = max over x_F of W_j.x (both under rho). Gate j is undecided under rho iff mn_j < t_j <= mx_j. Then P_t[undecided] = |{integers in (mn_j, mx_j]} intersect [-R,R]| / (2R+1) <= sum_{i in F} |W_ji| / (2R+1). For W_ji uniform on {-B,...,B}: E|W_ji| = B(B+1)/(2B+1), so E[undecided fraction] <= k B(B+1)/((2B+1)(2R+1)). With R = B sqrt(n) this is about k/(4 sqrt n): the sparse restriction shrinks the undecided fraction only when k = o(sqrt n).
structure.proved_step: Lemma (window bound for random thresholds): for every rho and F as above, P_t[gate j undecided] <= sum_{i in F}|W_ji|/(2R+1), with equality up to clipping at +-R. Proof: undecided iff f_j can be 1 and can be 0 under rho, i.e. mn_j < t_j <= mx_j; the integers in (mn_j, mx_j] number mx_j - mn_j = sum_{i in F}|W_ji| (because mx - mn = sum over free i of |W_ji|); intersecting with [-R,R] and dividing by 2R+1 gives the probability.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA-C1 (disjoint-support subclass, exact counting). Let f(x) = [sum_{j=1}^m v_j [w_j . x_{S_j} >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n, where the supports S_j are pairwise disjoint integer sets, |S_j| = k_j, w_j, t_j, v_j, T integers, V = sum_j |v_j|. Then #f = 2^{n - sum_j k_j} * sum over b in {0,1}^m with sum_j v_j b_j >= T of prod_j N_j(b_j), where N_j(b) = #{y in {0,1}^{S_j} : [w_j . y >= t_j] = b}. Proof: the blocks are disjoint, so the indicator variables [w_j . x_{S_j} >= t_j] are independent over uniform x; the free variables outside the union of supports contribute 2^{n - sum k_j}. Running-time algorithm: a DP over j with state s in [-V, V] (partial sum of v_j b_j), computing N_j by enumerating 2^{k_j} points; time O(sum_j 2^{k_j} k_j + m (2V+1) + n). Hence for k_j <= c log n and V <= poly(n), #f is computed in poly(n) time, versus 2^n for brute force. Exact-check: physalis_code_run cm-766064d60a724398 (400 random instances, n in [3,10], m <= 4, k_j <= 3, 0 mismatches vs brute force on the same instances); EXPLORATORY evidence only, not thr2_evaluate.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA-C2 (bounded-overlap conditioning, exact). Let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [w_j . x_{S_j} >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n with arbitrary integer supports S_j. Let occ(i) = #{j : i in S_j}, R = {i : occ(i) >= 2}, P_j = {i in S_j : occ(i) = 1}, free = #{i : occ(i) = 0}. Then #f = 2^{free} * sum over a in {0,1}^R of sum over b in {0,1}^m with sum_j v_j b_j >= T of prod_j N_j^a(b_j), where N_j^a(b) = #{y in {0,1}^{P_j} : [w_j . z = ... >= t_j] = b} with z the vector on S_j equal to a on S_j cap R and y on P_j. Proof: for fixed a, the indicator of block j is a function of y_{P_j} only; the sets P_j are pairwise disjoint, so the block indicators are independent under uniform y; summing over b with the threshold condition gives the formula, and summing over a and multiplying by 2^free gives #f. Running time: O(2^{|R|} (sum_j k_j 2^{|P_j|} + m (2V+1))) with V = sum_j |v_j|. Hence #f is computed faster than 2^n by a factor 2^{delta n} whenever |R| + max_j |P_j| <= (1-delta) n (up to poly factors).

structure.proved_step: LEMMA-HUB (restricted class, exact counting). Setting: n variables; hub set R with |R| = k; the other variables are partitioned into disjoint blocks P_1..P_G. Every bottom gate j has support(W_j) contained in R union P_g(j) for one block g(j); J_g = {j : g(j) = g}. Weights v_j are integers with V = sum_j |v_j| bounded by a polynomial in n. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} = sum over h in {0,1}^k of sum over s >= T of (D_{1,h} * ... * D_{G,h})(s), where D_{g,h}(s) = #{y in {0,1}^{P_g} : sum_{j in J_g} v_j [W_j.(h,y) >= t_j] = s} and * is convolution of integer distributions. PROOF: fix h. The outcomes of the gates in J_g depend only on y_g, and the blocks use disjoint variables, so the block sums are independent over the product set {0,1}^{P_1} x ... x {0,1}^{P_G}; the number of product points with total sum >= T is the convolution formula. RUNNING TIME: computing D_{g,h} takes 2^{|P_g|} evaluations of the gates in J_g, each O(n); the convolutions over the range [-V, V] cost O(G V^2). Total 2^k (sum_g 2^{|P_g|} n m + G V^2) <= poly(n, m, V) * 2^{k + max_g |P_g|}. So if k + max_g |P_g| <= (1 - delta) n and V <= poly(n), #SAT is computed in time poly(n) * 2^{(1-delta) n}.

structure.lemma: Scaled-threshold restriction lemma, repaired statement (no random fixed bits needed). Model: integer weights W_j in Z^n, F = free set with each variable free independently with prob p, fixed variables take ANY values a in {0,1}^{[n]\F}. Threshold t_j uniform on the integers of [-R_j, R_j], R_j = ceil(W_all,j/2), W_all,j = sum_i |w_ji|, independent of F and a. Then E_{F,t}[1(gate j undecided)] <= p for every integer weight vector.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. Fix F and a. Let c = sum over fixed i of w_i a_i, mn = sum over free i of min(0,w_i), mx = sum over free i of max(0,w_i). Over free x, w.x takes values in [mn+c, mx+c], so gate j is undecided iff mn+c < t <= mx+c. The number of integers t in that interval is exactly mx-mn = W_F := sum_{i in F}|w_i|, whatever c is. Since t is uniform on 2R+1 >= W_all+1 > W_all integers, P_t(undecided | F, a) <= W_F/(2R+1) <= W_F/W_all. Average over F: E_F[W_F] = p W_all (each |w_i| counted with prob p), so E_{F,a,t}[1(undecided)] <= p. The bound is independent of a, so the fixed bits may be arbitrary. Scope: random scaled thresholds, one gate. Adversarial thresholds are NOT covered (a fixed t can lie in the window for every F). The top gate is not decided and no running time is given.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (random restriction, +-1 weights, ANY fixed threshold). Let n>=2, w in {-1,+1}^n, 0<p<=1/4. Random restriction: each variable is free (in F) independently with prob p; for i not in F the bit a_i is uniform in {0,1}, independent of F. For a FIXED integer t, let mn = sum_i min(0,w_i a_i) over i not in F plus sum_{i in F} min(0,w_i), and mx analogously with max; gate undecided iff mn < t <= mx. Then P_{F,a}[undecided] <= 3*sqrt(2)*p*sqrt(n) (about 4.24 p sqrt n). PROOF. Fix F, let s=|F|, k=n-s. (1) mx-mn = s, so the set of values of base = sum_{i not in F} w_i a_i that make the gate undecided is a set of s consecutive integers. (2) Substitute b_i = 1-a_i for the k' indices with w_i=-1: base = sum_{w_i=+1} a_i + sum_{w_i=-1} b_i - const, a sum of k independent uniform bits plus a constant. (3) Sperner/Erdos: max_x P(Bin(k,1/2)=x) = C(k,floor(k/2))/2^k <= 1/sqrt(k) for k>=1 (even k: C(2m,m)/4^m <= 1/sqrt(pi m) <= 1/sqrt(2m); odd k: the extra factor (2m+1)/(2m+2) <= 1 and 1/sqrt(pi m) <= 1/sqrt(2m+1) for m>=1; k=1 gives 1/2). Hence P(undecided | F) <= min(1, s/sqrt(k)) for k>=1, and <= 1 for k=0. (4) Average over F. Region A = {s <= n/2}: k >= n/2, so s/sqrt(k) <= s*sqrt(2/n); E[s] = pn gives contribution <= p*sqrt(2n). Region B = {s > n/2}: its probability is <= sum over |F|>=n/2 of p^{|F|} <= 2^n p^{n/2} = p * (2^n p^{n/2-1}) <= p * 2^n * 4^{-(n/2-1)} = 4p (using p<=1/4 and n/2-1>=0). Total <= p*sqrt(2n) + 4p = p*sqrt(n)*(sqrt(2)+4/sqrt(n)) <= 3*sqrt(2)*p*sqrt(n) for n>=2. QED. NOTE: the window bound is for an ADVERSARIAL fixed t; the uniform-t version (proof-state lemma above) is weaker and elementary. The random-a assumption is needed: the OR-gate example with all fixed bits 0 (exact, cm-33cf0317f7794fa7) has P/p ~ 0.79 sqrt(n) at p=1/n, which is consistent with the bound.

structure.proved_step: CLAIMED S-R26-LEMMA-UNIFORM-THRESHOLD. Proof: fix F and a; let s = sum_{i notin F} w_i a_i, mn = s + sum_{i in F} min(0,w_i), mx = s + sum_{i in F} max(0,w_i). A linear form over the subcube attains its min and max at vertices, so over the subcube min = mn and max = mx. If mn >= t, g is constantly 1; if mx < t, g is constantly 0. Hence non-constant implies mn < t <= mx, and the integers t with mn < t <= mx number mx - mn = W_F := sum_{i in F}|w_i|. Since t is uniform on 2R+1 >= W+1 integers, P_t(nonconst | F,a) <= W_F/(W+1). Taking expectation, E[W_F] = p W, so the probability is at most p W/(W+1) < p. Conversely, if mn < t <= mx then both constant values are attained, so the events coincide. QED. Consequence: for m gates with independent uniform thresholds, E[#nonconstant gates] <= p sum_j W_j/(W_j+1) <= p m, by linearity.

structure.lemma: Random-threshold restriction lemma (weight-free). Let w in Z^n, W = sum_i |w_i|, R = ceil(W/2). Let F subset [n] with each i in F independently with probability p, and fix any a in {0,1}^{[n]\F}. Let t be uniform on the 2R+1 integers of [-R,R], independent of F and a. Let c = sum_{i not in F} w_i a_i. Then P_{F,t}[gate t <= w.x undecided under the restriction] <= p W/(2R+1) <= p.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. Fix F and a. Put mn = sum_{i in F} min(0,w_i), mx = sum_{i in F} max(0,w_i). Over the free variables, w.x - c takes values only in [mn, mx], so the gate is constant (always 1 if t <= mn+c, always 0 if t > mx+c). It is undecided iff mn+c < t <= mx+c. The half-open interval (mn+c, mx+c] contains exactly mx-mn = W_F := sum_{i in F}|w_i| integers. Since t is uniform on 2R+1 integers and independent of F, P_t[undecided | F, a] <= W_F/(2R+1). This bound is uniform in a. Taking expectation over F, E[W_F] = sum_i |w_i| P(i in F) = p W, so P_{F,t}[undecided] <= pW/(2R+1). Since 2R+1 >= W+1 > W (R = ceil(W/2)), the bound is at most p. If W = 0 both sides are 0. QED.

Then P_{F,a}[g(x) = [w.x >= t] is non-constant on the subcube x_i = a_i for i notin F] <= p(sqrt(2n) + 2) <= p(sqrt(2n)+4).
structure.proved_step: CLAIMED S-R26-LEMMA-UNIT-FIXED-THRESHOLD. Proof: fix F, k = |F|, m = n - k. Put s = sum_{i notin F} w_i a_i and mn = s + sum_{i in F} min(0,w_i), mx = s + sum_{i in F} max(0,w_i). The subcube minimum and maximum of w.x are mn and mx, so non-constancy is equivalent to mn < t <= mx, i.e. s lies in a set I_F of exactly mx - mn = k integers (all |w_i| = 1). (1) Distribution of s given F: s = sum_{w_i=+1} a_i + sum_{w_i=-1} (1-a_i) - N_- where N_- = #{i notin F: w_i=-1}; the terms a_i and 1-a_i are i.i.d. uniform bits, so s is a fixed integer shift of Bin(m,1/2). Hence each point probability is at most C(m,floor(m/2))/2^m <= sqrt(2/(pi m)) (standard central binomial bound, valid for all m >= 1). Therefore P_a(nonconst | F) <= min(1, k sqrt(2/(pi m))). (2) Case k <= n/2: then m >= n/2 >= 1/2, so sqrt(2/(pi m)) <= 2/sqrt(pi n) < sqrt(2/n), giving P_a(nonconst|F) <= k sqrt(2/n). Taking expectation, E[k 1(k<=n/2)] <= E[k] = pn, so this part contributes at most p sqrt(2n). (3) Case k > n/2: bound the conditional probability by 1; by Markov, P(k >= n/2) <= E[k]/(n/2) = 2p. Adding: P <= p sqrt(2n) + 2p. QED. Consequence: for m' gates with the same (F,a) law, E[#nonconstant gates] <= m' p(sqrt(2n)+2), by linearity, with no independence needed.

structure.lemma: Few-distinct-rows subclass (O2). Let n>=1, B>=1, and let W in Z^{m x n} have all entries in [-B,B] and at most r distinct rows, with distinct row set F = {F_1..F_r} (F_f in Z^n), row map sigma: [m] -> [r], thresholds t in Z^m, weights v in Z^m, T in Z. Let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] on x in {0,1}^n. Then #SAT(f) = sum over s in S of c(s) g(s), where S = {(F_f.x)_f : x in {0,1}^n}, c(s) = #{x : (F_f.x)_f = s}, g(s) = [sum_j v_j [s_{sigma(j)} >= t_j] >= T]. The DP over coordinates i = 1..n (c_{i+1}(s) = c_i(s) + c_i(s - F_{.,i+1})) computes c exactly, since the value vector after i coordinates depends only on x_1..x_i. Every coordinate of s lies in [-Bn, Bn], so |S| <= (2Bn+1)^r. Time: O((nr + m)(2Bn+1)^r) arithmetic operations, times a log factor for hashing. Hence for fixed r and B the count is poly(n, m). Corollary: if r*log2(2Bn+1) <= n/2 the time is 2^(n/2) * poly(n,m), a saving over brute force 2^n * m on this subclass.
structure.proved_step: CLAIMED (R-session lemma, not reviewed by this session): for the r-distinct-rows subclass with |W_ji| <= B, exact #SAT of THR o THR in time O((nr+m)(2Bn+1)^r) up to log factors; subclass 2^(n/2) poly whenever r log2(2Bn+1) <= n/2. Proof = the DP above, with induction on the coordinate index for correctness and the bound |S| <= (2Bn+1)^r for running time.

structure.lemma: Uniform-threshold restriction identity. Let W in Z^{1 x n} with S_+ = sum_j max(W_j,0), S_- = sum_j min(W_j,0), S = S_+ - S_- = sum_j |W_j|, lo = S_-, hi = S_+. Let t be uniform on the S+1 integers {lo,...,hi}. Fix x in {0,1}^n and a free set F. Let const = sum_{j not in F} W_j x_j, flo = const + sum_{j in F} min(W_j,0), fhi = const + sum_{j in F} max(W_j,0). The gate is undecided under the restriction iff flo < t <= fhi. Then P_t[undecided] = W_F/(S+1) exactly, where W_F = sum_{j in F}|W_j|. Averaging over a uniformly random free set F of size k: E_F[P_t[undecided]] = (k/n) S/(S+1) <= k/n.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. (i) flo >= lo, since const >= sum_{j notin F} min(W_j,0), so flo >= sum_j min(W_j,0) = lo. Likewise fhi <= hi. Hence (flo,fhi] lies inside [lo,hi] and contains exactly fhi - flo = W_F integers. (ii) t uniform on S+1 integers gives P = W_F/(S+1). (iii) Each j lies in a uniform k-subset F with probability k/n, so E_F[W_F] = (k/n) S, giving E_F P = (k/n) S/(S+1). The identity sum_F W_F = C(n-1,k-1) S is checked exactly in cm-26d396f198844b29 (276 sum checks, 0 mismatches), and the pointwise identity in 87576 checks, 0 mismatches. With k = c sqrt(n) this gives E_F P <= c/sqrt(n).

structure.proved_step: Lemma U (unit-weight fixed-threshold restriction). Let n>=2, 1<=k<=n-1, N=n-k, and let t in Z be ARBITRARY (worst case over thresholds). Let g(x)=[x_1+...+x_n >= t] on {0,1}^n. Fix a set F of k free coordinates and draw the N other coordinates i.i.d. uniform; set c = sum of the fixed coordinates, so c ~ Bin(N,1/2). Then P_c[g restricted to F is non-constant] <= k/sqrt(N). PROOF. The restricted function is c + (sum of the k free bits), which takes values in [c, c+k]. It is constant 1 iff c >= t and constant 0 iff c+k < t, so it is non-constant iff t-k <= c <= t-1, a window of at most k integers. Hence P <= sum over the window of P(Bin(N,1/2)=c) <= k * M_N, where M_N = max_j C(N,j)/2^N. Claim: M_N <= 1/sqrt(N) for all N>=1. Let a_m = C(2m,m)/4^m. (i) For N=2m, M_N = a_m. Put f(m)=a_m^2(3m+1), f(0)=1. Since a_{m+1}/a_m=(2m+1)/(2m+2), f(m+1)/f(m) <= 1 iff (2m+1)^2(3m+4) <= (2m+2)^2(3m+1); the difference RHS-LHS equals m >= 0. So a_m <= 1/sqrt(3m+1) <= 1/sqrt(2m) = 1/sqrt(N). (ii) For N=2m+1, M_N = C(2m+1,m)/2^{2m+1} = a_{m+1} (because C(2m+2,m+1)=2 C(2m+1,m)), so M_N <= 1/sqrt(3m+4) <= 1/sqrt(2m+1) = 1/sqrt(N). Combining, P <= k/sqrt(N). QED. COROLLARY: since N >= n/2 when k <= n/2, the bound is <= sqrt(2) k/sqrt(n); it shrinks with n only when k = o(sqrt n). SCOPE: unit weights only; uniform random fixed coordinates; the bound holds for every threshold t. It does NOT handle general integer weights (the Erdos-Moser/Halasz obstacle of G0002/G0004), the top gate, or running time. It is a special case of the open restriction obligation, not a closure of it.

structure.lemma: Fixed-threshold window lemma. Let w in Z^n with |w_j| <= B, let F subset [n] be the free set with k = |F|, let R = {j not in F : w_j != 0} with r = |R|, let t in Z be ANY fixed threshold, and let x_R be uniform on {0,1}^R (x_F arbitrary). Let g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t]. Then g depends on x_F, i.e. is undecided, iff c + minF < t <= c + maxF, where c = sum_{j in R} w_j x_j, minF = sum_{j in F} min(0,w_j), maxF = sum_{j in F} max(0,w_j). Its probability satisfies P[undecided] <= W_F * C(r, floor(r/2)) / 2^r <= W_F / sqrt(r) <= B k / sqrt(r), where W_F = sum_{j in F} |w_j| = maxF - minF. PROOF: (i) g is undecided iff the value at the all-max assignment of x_F (true) differs from the all-min one (false), which gives the stated interval for c. (ii) The interval [t-maxF, t-minF-1] contains exactly W_F integers. (iii) For each integer s, P(c = s) <= C(r,floor(r/2))/2^r: put y_j = x_j for w_j > 0 and y_j = 1 - x_j for w_j < 0; then c = const + sum_{j in R} |w_j| y_j, and the sets Y subset R with sum |w_j| over Y equal to a fixed value form an antichain (a strict subset has strictly smaller sum since |w_j| >= 1), so by Sperner there are at most C(r,floor(r/2)) of them. (iv) C(r,floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r) for r >= 1 (checked r = 1,2,3 directly; for even r = 2m the standard bound C(2m,m)/4^m <= 1/sqrt(pi m)). Union over the W_F integers gives the claim. Scope: integer weights, any fixed threshold, any free set, no distribution assumed on t; the bound is non-vacuous only when W_F = o(sqrt(r)). COROLLARY (expected count): for m gates with |w| <= B and a restriction leaving k free variables, E[#undecided] <= m B k / sqrt(n-k) (all weights nonzero), so if k <= sqrt(n-k)/(4B) the expected undecided fraction is <= 1/4. This re-derives the bounded-weight shrink already recorded (Theorem C, G0005) with the threshold distribution removed; it does NOT give the every-z or high-probability form, and it does NOT handle unbounded weights.

structure.lemma: CORRECTED CONVENTION (exploration, not a proved_step). Erdos Littlewood-Offord (|x_i|>=1, real): any open interval of length 2 contains at most C(N,floor(N/2)) of the 2^N signed sums sum eps_i x_i, eps_i in {+1,-1}. For integer weights w_i (nonzero) and S_F = subset sum over a uniform random subset F, S_F = (T + sum eps_i w_i)/2 with T = sum w_i, so any open interval of length 1 in S_F units contains at most central := C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N of the mass. Hence P[S_F in a window of k consecutive integers] <= k*central. The ceil(k/2) form is NOT the right consequence (refuted numerically, cm-8c35023bb8304a1e). Obstacle: for the restriction gate event the window width is R_F = sum over free j of |w_j| (not a constant k), so the bound gives R_F * central, which is o(1) only if R_F = o(sqrt N). The fixed-threshold shrink for general integer weights is therefore still OPEN (G0002).

structure.lemma: L1 (reformulation of 40a). Let M range over the uniform one-pass class of 40a. (i) Logical negation: NOT(40a) <=> exists M, c, d, m0 such that for all m >= m0: S_M(m) <= s(m)^c AND tau_M(m) <= s(m)^d. Proof: negate the prefix of 40a (forall M, forall c,d, forall m0, exists m>=m0 : S>s^c or tau>s^d) by de Morgan. (ii) Eventual versus all-length bounds: if such an M has the bounds only for m >= m0, define M' that runs M for m >= m0 and, for the finitely many m < m0, uses a fixed table of answers; for each fixed m < m0 the table has constant size (it depends only on m0 and s), so S_M'(m) <= s(m)^c' and tau_M'(m) <= s(m)^d' for all m with suitable constants c', d' (absorb the constant table into the polynomial via s(m) >= m). Hence 40a is equivalent to the 'all sufficiently large m' form of the MMW hypothesis that no poly-space, poly-update-time one-pass algorithm solves exact total Search-MCSP^A[s]. Caveat for (ii): this needs s(m) >= m and the table size to be bounded by a constant independent of the machine's own s-dependence; I checked the case form only, not the uniformity conditions of [4].

structure.lemma: r-packing bound: G without isolated vertices, E=A disjoint-union B, D=V(A) cap V(B), M0 a perfect matching, C_1..C_r pairwise vertex-disjoint M0-alternating cycles, each X_i = side-changing D-vertices of C_i nonempty. Then the 2^r signatures sigma(M0 xor union_{i in S} E(C_i)), S subset [r], are pairwise distinct elements of Sigma (boundary signatures of perfect matchings), so |Sigma| >= 2^r for every r.
structure.proved_step: CLAIMED (haiku-5-5, not independent). Proof: (1) M_S = M0 xor union_{i in S} E(C_i) is a perfect matching, since cycles are vertex-disjoint and alternating. (2) For v in D: if v lies on no cycle of S its matched edge is unchanged; if v lies on C_i with i in S, its matched edge switches to the other cycle edge at v, which changes side exactly when v in X_i. Hence sigma(M_S) = sigma(M0) xor 1_{union_{i in S} X_i}. (3) X_i are nonempty and pairwise disjoint, so the indicators 1_{union_{S} X_i} are distinct for distinct S; XOR with sigma(M0) preserves distinctness. Hence 2^r distinct signatures in Sigma and |Sigma| >= 2^r.

structure.lemma: Reuse-elimination (naive): for an acyclic De Morgan circuit C with S non-input gates and r gates of fan-out >= 2, f_C has a De Morgan formula with at most 2^r * 2S leaves. Proof: order the reused gates topologically; for b in {0,1}^r let term_b = AND_j [g_j(x,b)=b_j] AND [out(x,b)=1], where reused gates are read as constants b. Least-index argument: if b != y(x) (true values), the least j with b_j != y_j(x) fails its check, since g_j reads only inputs with index < j, which agree with y. So exactly one term is consistent and OR_b term_b = f_C. Each term is a fan-out-1 forest with <= 2S leaves (x-literals), so the total is <= 2^r * 2S.
structure.proved_step: Naive reuse-elimination bound L(f_C) <= 2^r * 2S for acyclic De Morgan C (hand proof above; finite check cm-833b4c80d7204c04 agrees on sampled circuits)

structure.lemma: Let W = U A + E over Z with U in Z^{m x r}, A in Z^{r x n}, |A_ic| <= a, and E supported on a column set S with |S| = s <= k, where k is the number of nonzero entries of E. Let F = [n] minus S. For x in {0,1}^n, the row-j dot product is U_j . y(x_F) + sum_{c in S} W_jc x_c with y(x_F) = A_F x_F in Z^r, since W_jc = sum_i U_ji A_ic on F. The count #{x : sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T} equals the sum over x_S in {0,1}^s of the number of x_F weighted by the value of y, so it is computed exactly by a DP over F with state y, of size at most (2a n + 1)^r, repeated for each x_S. Time 2^s (2an+1)^r poly(m,n) <= 2^k (2an+1)^r poly(m,n). This is a re-derivation of S0002 and does not close G0001(i) for k = Theta(n) or for rank r = Theta(n / log n).

structure.lemma: Cut lemma. Let C be a Boolean circuit (fan-in <= 2, gates AND/OR/XOR/NOT) on inputs x_1..x_n, and let (A,B) be a partition of the input variables. Let the gates be split into sides S_A and S_B (each gate on the side it is assigned), and let kappa be the number of wires (gate-input edges, including input-variable edges) whose endpoints lie on different sides. Let M be the 2^|A| x 2^|B| communication matrix of f = C, with rows indexed by a in {0,1}^A and columns by b in {0,1}^B. Then log2 rank_R(M) <= kappa + 1.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. Each cross wire carries one bit from its source side to its target side. Evaluate C in topological order: a gate on side S_A needs only values from S_A or from cross wires; the value of a cross wire is a function of its source side's inputs and bits already received, so it is sent once, by its source party, as one bit. Each cross wire contributes at most one bit, so the transcript has at most kappa bits. Once all cross wires are transmitted, both parties know the output bit for their input pair; the party holding the output gate sends one more bit, so the total is at most kappa+1 bits. A deterministic protocol with c bits has at most 2^c leaves; each leaf is a combinatorial rectangle on which the output is constant, so M is a sum of at most 2^c rank-one 0/1 matrices, rank_R(M) <= 2^c. Hence log2 rank <= kappa+1. The argument uses only the wire count, not any gate structure, and it holds for any partition of gates. Remark: the lab check uses the 0-based side assignment and counts each gate input once, matching the wire count above.

structure.proved_step: L-K1-PREFIX (closes G0005(a) for the prefix-cut family). Setting: f:{0,1}^N->{0,1} computed by a fan-in<=2 circuit C with gates G, inputs x_1..x_N in a fixed order. Define P(x_j)=j and P(g)=max of P over the inputs of gate g (so P(u)<=P(g) along every wire u->g, and 1<=P(v)<=N). Let W = number of wires (gate-input edges), Lambda(C)=sum over wires u->g of (P(g)-P(u)). For i in [1,N-1], M_i = communication matrix of f for A={x_1..x_i}, B=rest. CLAIM: (1) sum_{i=1}^{N-1} log2 rank_R(M_i) <= (N-1) + Lambda(C); (2) Lambda(C) <= W(N-1) <= 2|G|(N-1); hence for every input order, |G| >= (sum_i log2 rank_R(M_i) - (N-1)) / (2(N-1)). PROOF. Let L_i={v: P(v)<=i}. Input x_j is in L_i iff j<=i, so L_i restricted to inputs is exactly A. If g in L_i and u->g is a wire, P(u)<=P(g)<=i so u in L_i: no wire goes from the right side to the left side. Hence the cross wires for cut i are exactly the wires with P(u)<=i<P(g); call their number kappa_i. This is a legal gate split for (A,B), so S0001 (SURVIVED_REVIEW) gives log2 rank_R(M_i) <= kappa_i+1. Summing over i: sum_i kappa_i = sum over wires of #{i in [1,N-1]: P(u)<=i<P(g)} = sum over wires of (P(g)-P(u)), because 1<=P(u) and P(g)<=N. So the sum is <= Lambda(C)+(N-1). (2) holds since 0<=P(g)-P(u)<=N-1 and each gate has at most 2 wires. Corollary (CEILING): rank_R(M_i) <= 2^{min(i,N-i)}, so sum_i log2 rank <= N^2/4 and the bound gives |G| >= (N^2/4-(N-1))/(2(N-1)) = N/8 - O(1) at most. The method cannot give a superlinear bound for any N-input function using prefix cuts.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (subclass, cut width). Fix a variable order pi and a level l. Call a node prefix-side if its support lies in the first l variables. Let kappa_l be the number of prefix-side nodes with an edge into a non-prefix-side gate. Then the level width K_l (number of distinct residual functions C restricted to rho, for rho in {0,1}^l) satisfies K_l <= 2^kappa_l, because each non-prefix-side gate's value under rho depends on rho only through the constant values of the kappa_l crossing nodes. Hence the OBDD size for order pi is at most sum_l 2^kappa_l. COROLLARY: if kappa_l <= c log n for all l, then #SAT of C runs in poly(n, m) time by building the OBDD. This is the standard cut-width / OBDD-width technique and is not new; it is recorded only as a verified subclass.

structure.lemma: Single-order residual-width sum (identity order). C is a fan-in-2 circuit over x_0..x_{n-1} with gates G, output node out, computing f. For a node v let t(v) = bit_length of its support bitmask, so t(v) = 1 + max variable index in the support. Let Lambda(C) = sum over wires u->g of max(0, t(g) - t(u)). For l = 0..n let K_l = number of distinct residual functions f restricted to x_{<l} = rho, over rho in {0,1}^l. Then sum_{l=0}^{n} log2 K_l <= Lambda(C) + #{l : t(out) <= l}. Proof: fix l and P = {0..l-1}. Let X_l be the set of prefix-side nodes (support inside P) that feed a non-prefix gate. By the S0026 argument, if out is non-prefix then K_l <= 2^{|X_l|}; if out is prefix-side then K_l <= 2. Since supports grow along wires, t(g) >= t(u) for every wire u->g. Each w in X_l has a wire w->g with t(w) <= l < t(g), so |X_l| <= #{wires u->g : t(u) <= l < t(g)}. Summing over l, each wire with t(u) < t(g) is counted exactly t(g)-t(u) times, so sum_l |X_l| <= Lambda(C). Adding the at most one bit per level where out is prefix-side gives the claim. Scope: a single fixed variable order; Lambda depends on the order and can be about |C| * N for a bad order.

structure.lemma: REPAIRED CUT LEMMA (single partition, input-wire crossings counted). Let C be a fan-in-2 circuit over inputs x_0..x_{N-1}, and split the inputs into A (Alice) and B (Bob). Owner rule: each input node belongs to the holder of its variable; each gate belongs to Alice or Bob (arbitrary). Let kappa = number of wires u->g, including input wires, whose endpoints have different owners. Let f be the output and M_f the 2^|A| x 2^|B| communication matrix. Then log2 rank_Q(M_f) <= kappa+1. PROOF: the protocol runs in topological order; a node's owner computes it, and when the other party needs a node's value it is sent as one bit on that crossing wire. Total bits <= kappa, plus 1 bit announcing the output: c <= kappa+1. For a fixed transcript t, Alice's messages depend only on a and t, and Bob's only on b, so the set R_t of inputs producing t is a combinatorial rectangle S_t x T_t on which f is constant. The leaves partition all inputs, so M_f = sum over 1-leaves of the indicator matrices of R_t; each is rank 1 over Q, hence rank_Q(M_f) <= #1-leaves <= 2^(kappa+1). SCOPE: one fixed partition, deterministic protocol, any field. It is a standard log-rank bound and does NOT give any aggregate over partitions (G0001, G0002 stay open). S0001 (gate-only kappa) is superseded: IP_2 with all gates Alice's has gate-only kappa = 0 but rank 3 > 2. Evidence: cm-3d0d3280c99e4c9b (0 violations, 3000 random circuits, input crossings included). Hand proof is the argument above and needs an independent review.

structure.lemma: REPAIR of the prefix-cut route (refuted by S0046 on expander-like circuits). Setup: C is a fan-in<=2 circuit with nodes = inputs x_1..x_n and gates, edges = wires u->g, output o. For a prefix length l, let P be a set of nodes that is closed under predecessors (g in P and u->g a wire imply u in P) and whose inputs are exactly x_1..x_l. Let w(P) = number of wires u->g with u in P and g not in P. Claim: the number of distinct subfunctions f(a,.), a in {0,1}^l, is at most 2^(w(P)). Hence the OBDD for the order x_1..x_n has size at most sum_l 2^(w_l), where w_l is the boundary of a closed prefix set at level l.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. (1) By induction over a topological order, every node in P has a value that depends only on a, since P is closed under predecessors. (2) Let W be the set of wires leaving P; |W| = w(P). For any node outside P, its value is a function of its own inputs, which are either suffix inputs, outside gates, or wires in W. So for each suffix assignment b there is a function G_b with f(a,b) = G_b(z(a)), where z(a) in {0,1}^W lists the values carried by the wires in W. (3) Therefore f(a,.) = G_(.)(z(a)) is determined by z(a), which takes at most 2^(w(P)) values, so at most 2^(w(P)) distinct subfunctions occur. QED. Consequence: if every level l admits a closed prefix set with w_l <= W, then the OBDD has size at most n 2^W and #SAT of C takes time about n 2^W poly(s). For W = O(log s) this is polynomial.

Proof: Case o not in P: by induction over topological order, each node outside P is a function of (b, z(a)), so f(a,b)=G_b(z(a)) and K <= 2^w. Case o in P: then f(a,b)=val_o(a) does not depend on b, so f(a,.) is one of the two constants 0, 1 and K <= 2 <= 2^(w+1). Hence K <= 2^(w+[o in P]) for all cases, matching cm-b15c73c3c24a4cf4 (0 violations). Consequence: OBDD size for the order x_1..x_n is at most sum_l 2^(w_l+1) <= 2 n 2^W when all closed prefix boundaries have w_l <= W; polynomial for W = O(log s).

structure.lemma: SHARP CUT LEMMA (one split). Circuit C of fan-in 2, inputs x (Alice, h bits) and y (Bob, the rest); every gate is assigned to Alice or Bob. X = set of Alice-side nodes (inputs or gates) read by at least one Bob-side gate. Claim: log2 rank_Q M_f <= |X|.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. Case 1, output on Bob's side. Induction in topological order: every Bob-side node value is a function of (y, z(x)), where z(x) in {0,1}^X is the vector of values of X-nodes (a Bob gate reads Bob nodes or X-nodes only). So row M[x,.] depends only on z(x); there are at most 2^|X| distinct rows, and rank <= number of distinct rows. Case 2, output on Alice's side: f(x,y) = out(x) does not depend on y, so rank <= 1. Hence log2 rank <= |X|. TIGHTNESS: f = AND_i NOT(x_i AND y_i) (disjointness), h = m, Bob reads each x_i, |X| = m, and M_f is the m-fold tensor power of [[1,1],[1,0]] (det -1), so rank = 2^m and log2 rank = m = |X|. The +1 in the earlier statement is slack, not needed.

structure.lemma: L1 (one-way cut bound). C: Boolean circuit, fan-in <= 2, gates AND/OR/XOR/NOT, inputs x in {0,1}^a and y in {0,1}^b, f = output node. Split all nodes into sides A, B with every x-input in A, every y-input in B, and no edge from a B-node into an A-gate. kappa := number of A-nodes having a consumer in B (x-inputs count). Then rank_Q M_f <= 2^kappa, hence log2 rank_Q M_f <= kappa < kappa+1.
structure.proved_step: PROOF OF L1. (i) By induction on topological order, every A-node is a function of x alone: x-inputs trivially; an A-gate's inputs are A-nodes because no B-node feeds an A-gate. (ii) Let S(x) in {0,1}^kappa be the values of the kappa cross nodes (A-nodes with a B-consumer), which are functions of x by (i). By induction every B-node is a function of (y, S(x)): its inputs are y-inputs, B-nodes, or A-nodes, and any A-node feeding a B-node is a cross node, hence a coordinate of S(x). So f(x,y) = G(S(x), y) for some G. If the output node is an A-node, then f = h(x) and M_f has rank <= 1 <= 2^kappa. (iii) For s in {0,1}^kappa let u_s be the indicator vector of {x : S(x) = s} and w_s(y) = G(s,y). Then M_f = sum over s of u_s w_s^T, a sum of at most 2^kappa rank-<=1 matrices over Q, so rank_Q M_f <= 2^kappa. QED.

structure.lemma: L2 (two-way cut bound, repairs the gap of L1). C: Boolean circuit, fan-in <= 2, gates AND/OR/XOR/NOT; inputs x in {0,1}^a, y in {0,1}^b; f = output node. Partition all nodes into sides A and B with x-inputs in A and y-inputs in B; edges may go in both directions. K = set of nodes having a consumer on the other side, kappa = |K|. Then rank_Q M_f <= 2^(kappa+1), hence log2 rank_Q M_f <= kappa+1.
structure.proved_step: PROOF OF L2. Fix a topological order v_1,...,v_N of the circuit. Let c_1,...,c_kappa be the nodes of K in that order; each c_i is owned by Alice (A) or Bob (B). Protocol: for i = 1..kappa the owner of c_i sends the bit value(c_i), then the output owner sends f's bit if f is not in K, i.e. at most kappa+1 bits. Well-defined and deterministic: the speaker sequence depends only on the circuit and the side assignment, not on the inputs. Correctness: when the owner of c_i speaks, it knows its own input and all bits sent so far, and it can compute c_i. Induction on the topological order: any input of c_i is either an input node (owned by the speaker, since inputs lie on their own side), a node on the speaker's side (computed by the speaker by induction), or a node on the other side with a consumer on the speaker's side, hence in K, hence earlier in the order and already sent. So value(c_i) is a function of the speaker's input and the transcript so far. Thus the transcript determines all of K and f. Rectangles: for a fixed transcript tau, the set of x with tau consistent is a set X_tau, and similarly Y_tau for y; by the standard induction over rounds the set {(x,y): transcript = tau} equals X_tau x Y_tau. On a leaf f is constant (it is determined by tau). Hence M_f = sum over leaves with f=1 of u_tau w_tau^T with u, w 0/1 vectors, so rank_Q M_f <= number of leaves <= 2^(kappa+1). QED. Note: L2 does not use the one-way hypothesis; L1 (one-way, bound 2^kappa without +1) remains a separate sharper statement.

structure.lemma: CUT LEMMA: Let C be a fan-in-2 circuit over inputs X = A u B, and let sigma assign every input and gate to side A or B. Let kappa = number of edges u->v with sigma(u) != sigma(v) (both directions, input edges included). Then for the communication matrix M_f of f = C with A-inputs as rows and B-inputs as columns, rank_R M_f <= 2^(kappa+1), i.e. log2 rank_R M_f <= kappa+1.
structure.proved_step: Proof: Alice and Bob process gates in topological order. Each cross edge carries one bit, sent by the side that owns its source once the source value is determined from that side's inputs and previously received bits. Total communication is at most kappa bits. The output bit adds 1, so the deterministic communication complexity satisfies D(f) <= kappa+1. A deterministic protocol of depth d partitions the matrix into at most 2^d monochromatic rectangles, each of rank at most 1, so rank_R M_f <= 2^d. Hence log2 rank_R M_f <= kappa+1.

structure.proved_step: Proof: Protocol: each cross edge carries the value of its source gate, sent by the owner of the source once that value is determined. Each gate is evaluated by the side that owns it, using its own inputs and bits received so far. Total communication is exactly kappa bits, so the protocol tree has at most 2^kappa leaves. For each leaf, the set of (a,b) reaching it is a combinatorial rectangle R_l on which f is constant. M_f = sum over 1-leaves of the indicator matrices of R_l. Each indicator of a rectangle has real rank at most 1, so rank_R(M_f) <= number of 1-leaves <= 2^kappa. Hence log2 rank_R(M_f) <= kappa.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (single split, standard): for a circuit C on X∪Y with κ wires from X-side nodes into Y-side gates, M[a,b]=C(a,b) has at most 2^κ distinct rows, so rank_Q M ≤ 2^κ and log2 rank_Q M ≤ κ. Proof: row a is determined by w(a) ∈ {0,1}^κ (crossing-wire values), since C(a,b)=D(w(a),b) for the Y-subcircuit D; equal w gives equal rows; rank ≤ number of distinct rows.

structure.refuted_approach: S0078 (single-split lemma, kappa = X->Y wires only) is FALSE as stated. Counterexample: IP_2 = a1b1+a2b2 mod 2 with all gates on Alice's side. kappa_XtoY = 0, but M has 4 distinct rows and rank_Q = 3 > 2^0. Cause: the Y-side wires do not enter the row-determination argument; a row is not determined by the X->Y crossing values when Y->X edges exist. Repair: count ALL cross edges, kappa_all = #{edges (u,g): side(u) != side(g)}, and rank_Q M <= 2^(kappa_all+1). This is the statement of S0044 (claimed by R1281, not yet reviewed by another model family). label: G0041
statement: G0001 (aggregate over partitions) remains open. Sharpened obstacle: the single-order prefix route (L-K1-PREFIX, sum_i log2 rank_i <= (N-1) + Lambda_pi(C)) cannot be repaired by minimising over orders alone, because for a bounded-degree expander-shaped circuit graph on s vertices every order has Lambda_pi = Omega(s^2) (MINLA lower bound, S0046), which exceeds polylog(N)*s once s is polynomial in N. Any repair must therefore use a partition family that is not a prefix family of one order (e.g. a recursive balanced-separator family adapted to C), or drop the requirement that the aggregate be linear in |C|. structure.lemma: One-directional cut bound: if all edges between L and R go from L to R and there are kappa of them, then the rank over Q of the communication matrix of the output (rows x_L, columns x_R) is at most 2^kappa. Proof: by induction on topological order, every R-gate value is a function of x_R and the kappa cross-edge tail values, which are functions of x_L; so f(x_L,x_R)=g(w(x_L),x_R) with w in {0,1}^kappa, giving at most 2^kappa distinct rows.

structure.proved_step: GENERAL-WEIGHT ALIVE-SURVIVAL LEMMA (integer weights, S0007). Setting: w_ji, t_j integers; A subset [n], |A|=k, F=[n]\A, f=n-k; z uniform on {0,1}^F; L_j = sum_{i in A} min(0,w_ji), U_j = sum_{i in A} max(0,w_ji), S_j(z) = sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i, f_j = #{i in F : w_ji != 0}, N(A,z) = #{j : T_j restricted to x_F=z is non-constant on {0,1}^A}. Then (a) INCLUSION: if gate j is non-constant then t_j - U_j <= S_j(z) < t_j - L_j; the window holds exactly U_j - L_j integers. (b) For f_j >= 1: Pr_z[j non-constant] <= (U_j - L_j)/sqrt(f_j). (c) E_z[N(A,z)] <= sum_{j: f_j>=1} (U_j-L_j)/sqrt(f_j) + #{j : f_j = 0 and t_j - U_j <= 0 < t_j - L_j}. PROOF. (a) The restricted gate is [R_j(x_A) >= t_j - S_j(z)] with R_j = sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i, whose values lie in [L_j, U_j]. Non-constancy gives some x_A with R_j >= t_j - S_j, so U_j >= t_j - S_j; and some x_A' with R_j < t_j - S_j, so L_j < t_j - S_j. These are the two inequalities. Integrality gives the count U_j-L_j. (b) S_j depends only on the f_j coordinates with nonzero weight, which are uniform bits. Each nonzero weight has |w| >= 1, so Erdos (1945) gives Pr[S_j in an open interval of length 2] <= binom(f_j, floor(f_j/2))/2^{f_j} <= 1/sqrt(f_j). Summing over the U_j-L_j integers in the window gives (b). (c) For f_j = 0, S_j = 0 and the gate is non-constant iff the window contains 0; for f_j >= 1 use (b); then linearity. QED. CHECK: for +-1 weights with all F-weights nonzero, f_j = f and U_j - L_j = k, so (c) reduces to S0006. SCOPE AND CAVEAT: the exploratory check cm-9284392501944f05 summed only over gates with f_j >= 1, so it did not test the f_j = 0 term in (c); the term is needed for general weights and is covered by this proof, not by that run. Progress: bookkeeping. The bound is in expectation, costs 2^k per surviving gate, and closes no obligation (G0001, G0002, G0007 stay OPEN).

structure.lemma: CONSTRUCTIVE RE-DERIVATION OF S0006(b) WITH EXPLICIT CONSTANT. Setting as in the ALIVE-SURVIVAL LEMMA: w_ji in {-1,+1} for i in A and for i in F, |A|=k, |F|=f=n-k>=1, z uniform in {0,1}^F, S_j(z)=sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i. Claim: P_z[gate j non-constant on {0,1}^A] <= k/sqrt(f), hence E_z[N(A,z)] <= m k/sqrt(n-k). Proof: (1) Non-constancy window: L_j+S_j <= t_j-1 < U_j+S_j is equivalent to t_j-U_j <= S_j < t_j-L_j, an integer window with U_j-L_j = k integers (since |w|=1 on A). (2) Sign flip: put y_i = z_i if w_ji=+1 and y_i = 1-z_i if w_ji=-1 (i in F). Then y is uniform on {0,1}^F and S_j = Y - c_j with Y = sum y_i ~ Bin(f,1/2) and c_j an integer. (3) So P[S_j in a window of k integers] = sum over those k integers s of P[Y = s + c_j] <= k * max_r C(f,r)/2^f = k * C(f, floor(f/2))/2^f <= k/sqrt(f) (central binomial bound, valid for all f>=1). (4) Linearity of expectation over j gives E_z N <= m k/sqrt(n-k). (5) Averaging gives the deterministic EXISTENCE statement: some z in {0,1}^F has N(A,z) <= m k/sqrt(n-k). Scope: +-1 weights only. For this lemma the existence form is a choice of z by averaging, not an algorithm.

Claim: E_z[N(A,z)] <= sum_j (U_j - L_j) * a_j, where a_j = C(f_j, floor(f_j/2))/2^{f_j} <= 1/sqrt(f_j) whenever f_j >= 1. structure.proved_step: PROCEDURE R2 (deterministic restriction by conditional expectations; repair of the refuted every-z form). Setting as in S0006: w_ji in {-1,+1}, |A|=k, f=n-k>=1, S_j(z)=sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i. Since the non-constancy of gate j on {0,1}^A depends only on the offset S_j(z) (A-weights and t_j are fixed), N(A,z) = #{j : S_j(z) in W_j}, where W_j is a set of at most k integers (S0006 step 1). Let F_r(p) = sum_j P[S_j in W_j | first r bits of z equal p], for a prefix p of length r. Then (i) F_r(p) = (F_{r+1}(p0)+F_{r+1}(p1))/2; (ii) each F_r(p) is an exact finite sum: given p, S_j = a_j(p) + (signed Bin(f-r,1/2)), so P[S_j in W_j | p] = sum over s in W_j of the binomial pmf at the shifted index. Algorithm: start with the empty prefix; at each of the f steps append the bit b minimising F_{r+1}(pb). By (i), F is non-increasing along the path, so the output z* satisfies N(A,z*) = F_f(z*) <= F_0 = sum_j P[S_j in W_j] <= m k / sqrt(f) (S0006). Running time: f steps, each O(m k f) exact arithmetic (rational with denominator 2^f, or exact integers), so poly(n, m). Scope: +-1 weights; the output is ONE restriction z*, not a CAPP algorithm.

statement: Correction to the cost-model consequence recorded with R2 (G0013). The union bound gives Pr_z[N>=1] <= E N <= m k/sqrt(n-k). For k=1 this is m/sqrt(n-1). For any polynomial m = n^c the union bound gives only n^{c-1/2} = n^{-Omega(1)}, so it yields no 2^n/n^{omega(1)} saving at all. structure.lemma: DERANDOMISED SURVIVOR COUNT (+-1 weights, fixed A). Let A, F partition [n], |A| = k >= 1, f = n - k >= 1, weights w_ji in {-1,+1} for all i, thresholds T_j in Z, j = 1..m. For z in {0,1}^F let g_j(x,z) = [sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i + sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i >= T_j] on x in {0,1}^A, and N(z) = #{j : g_j(.,z) non-constant on {0,1}^A}. Then there is z* in {0,1}^F, computable in O(m f^3) integer operations by the method of conditional expectations, with N(z*) <= E_z[N(z)] <= m k / sqrt(f). PROOF: (1) Window. Let L = sum_{A} min(0,w_ji), U = sum_{A} max(0,w_ji). Since |w| = 1 on A, {sum_A w_ji x_i} = all integers in [L,U], so U - L = k. With S = sum_F w_ji z_i, g_j is non-constant iff L+S < T_j <= U+S, i.e. S lies in an integer window of exactly k integers. (2) Coin flip. Put y_i = z_i if w_ji = +1, y_i = 1 - z_i if w_ji = -1. Then y is uniform on {0,1}^F and S = Y - c_j with Y ~ Bin(f,1/2), c_j in Z. So P[S in window] <= k * max_r P[Y=r] = k C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= k/sqrt(f) (central binomial bound, valid for f >= 1). Summing over j: E_z N <= m k/sqrt(f). (3) Conditional expectations. For a prefix p of length r, E_p = E[N | z_1..z_r = p]; then E_p = (E_{p0} + E_{p1})/2, so one of the two children does not exceed E_p. Greedily fixing z_{r+1} to the smaller child yields z* with N(z*) <= E_root. Each E_p is exact: given p, S_j = (fixed part) + sum of f - r independent +-1-coin terms, whose law is a DP over integer sums in [-f,f], costing O(m f^2) per evaluation; total O(m f^3). Scope: +-1 weights only; A fixed in advance (not chosen adaptively); z* is one restriction, not a CAPP algorithm.

structure.proved_step: INTEGER-WEIGHT SURVIVOR LEMMA (G0009(b)). Setting: A, F partition [n], |A| = k >= 1, f = |F| >= 1, integer weights w_ji with |w_ji| >= 1 for i in F (zero weights on A allowed), thresholds T_j in Z, gates g_j(x,z) = [sum_A w_ji x_i + sum_F w_ji z_i >= T_j] on x in {0,1}^A, z in {0,1}^F. Let M_j = sum_{i in A} |w_ji| and N(z) = #{j : g_j(., z) non-constant}. CLAIM: (i) for each j, #{z : g_j(., z) non-constant} <= M_j * C(f, floor(f/2)); hence P_z[non-constant] <= M_j / sqrt(f). (ii) E_z N(z) <= (sum_j M_j)/sqrt(f) <= m k B / sqrt(f) if |w| <= B on A. (iii) The conditional-expectation fixing of Lemma S-DERAND gives z* with N(z*) <= E_z N. PROOF. (1) Window: g_j is non-constant iff min_x (A-sum) + S < T_j <= max_x (A-sum) + S, where S = sum_F w_ji z_i. This holds for any integer weights, with no gap condition. With L = sum_A min(0,w_ji) and U = sum_A max(0,w_ji), non-constancy is equivalent to T_j - U <= S <= T_j - L - 1. This is an integer window with exactly U - L = M_j integers. (2) Point masses: put eps_i = 2 z_i - 1 in {-1,+1}. Then S = s iff sum_F w_ji eps_i = 2s - sum_F w_ji. Since |w_ji| >= 1, Erdos's Littlewood-Offord theorem (1945: for reals |b_i| >= 1, an open interval of length 2 contains at most C(f, floor(f/2)) of the 2^f sums sum eps_i b_i) gives #{z : S = s} <= C(f, floor(f/2)) for every integer s. (3) Union: #{z : S in window} <= sum over the M_j window integers of #{z : S = s} <= M_j C(f, floor(f/2)). Dividing by 2^f and using C(f, floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f) (f >= 1) gives (i). Summing over j gives (ii). (4) Step (iii) uses only that N is an integer-valued function whose expectation is known; the DP for E_p has integer sums in [-fB, fB], so it costs O(m f^2 B) per evaluation and O(m f^3 B) in total. SCOPE: non-zero integer weights on F, arbitrary integers on A, fixed A. Zero weights on F reduce f to f' = #nonzero F-weights, giving 1/sqrt(f'). The ±1 lemma S0006 is the case M_j = k. The lemma says nothing about all z simultaneously, adaptive A, or Chen-Williams 2019.

structure.lemma: INTEGER-WEIGHT WINDOW LEMMA (extends S0006 from +-1 to integer weights; gap G0007(i)). Fix a gate j with integer weights a_i (i in A, |a_i| >= 1, |A| = k) and b_i (i in F, b_i in Z, f' = #{i in F : b_i != 0} >= 1). Let U = sum_A max(0,a_i), L = sum_A min(0,a_i), B = U - L = sum_A |a_i|. For z in {0,1}^F let S(z) = sum_F b_i z_i and N_j(z) = [g_j(.,z) non-constant on {0,1}^A], g_j(x,z) = [sum_A a_i x_i + S(z) >= T]. Then (i) P_{z uniform}[N_j(z)=1] <= B / sqrt(f'). Proof: (1) Non-constancy needs L + S < T <= U + S, so S lies in an integer window of exactly B integers. (2) Sperner: flip y_i = 1 - z_i for b_i < 0 and y_i = z_i otherwise; then S = sum_{F'} |b_i| y_i + const, y uniform on {0,1}^{F'}. Two subsets T1 strictly contained in T2 have sums differing by >= 1, so the level sets {y : sum |b_i| y_i in an open interval of length 1} form an antichain; hence #{y : S = r} <= C(f', floor(f'/2)) and P[S = r] <= C(f',floor(f'/2))/2^{f'} <= 1/sqrt(f') (central binomial bound, f' >= 1). (3) Union over the B window integers. Hence E_z N_j(z) <= B/sqrt(f'). Summing over j: E_z N(z) <= sum_j B_j / sqrt(f'_j). For |a| = 1 this is k/sqrt(f') and recovers S0006. For weights bounded by W, B_j <= k W, so E_z N(z) <= m k W / sqrt(f_min). Derandomisation: the conditional-expectation fixing of S0006 applies unchanged, since each E_p is an exact DP over integer sums in [-W f, W f] (cost O(m f * W f) per evaluation). Scope: integer weights, A fixed in advance, expectation (not deterministic) bound for all z.
